1.14.0: A picture dragged onto a slide that has text now sits beside the text, in a new Text + picture layout.
Drag several pictures in at once and each gets its own slide. Let a picture go on any slide in the list on the left to put it there.
New Full picture layout: the picture fills the whole slide.
1.13.0: Present a lesson from the Planner, or from Today when its class is on now or next: its slides fill the screen, and the arrow keys or a clicker move through them.
While presenting, A shows the agenda to tick off, T starts a timer the class can see, N shows your notes and B blanks the screen.
The bar shows how many minutes the class has left, from your timetable.
After a lesson is taught, one line says where the class got to. It shows on the lesson and on the week, and presenting again picks up there.
1.12.0: A returned paper starts with a feedback page: the score, each rubric row with the level given and what that level means, your comment, and every comment on the paper with its page number.
It is on unless you turn it off under Options on the Return tab. Your own pages are not changed, and bringing an export back in opens only those.
1.11.0: The Planner’s sections are in the sidebar: Calendar, Units, Past lessons, Activities and Rubrics. The row of tabs across the top is gone.
A lesson has a lighter top: its name, its classes, its status and Download. Copy for Claude, Versions, the upload and the links are under More.
Comments shows above a lesson once it has one.
1.7.0: Home is now Today: the classes you teach today with the lesson planned for each, the papers waiting to be marked, and the papers ready to hand back.
What the class needs next: after a set of papers is scored, Today shows the weakest rubric row and how many students to sit down with.
A class page is quieter. Click anywhere on an assignment’s row to open it; the only blue button is the one that adds an assignment.
Forget, and the other ways to open papers, moved into the ⋯ menu on each row.
1.6.0: A new browser opens on three questions (your classes, how you grade, where work is kept) and starts with nothing of anyone else’s in it.
A sample class of made-up students, with papers to mark, for trying things out. Remove it from Home when you’re done.
The app uses the name of your own school system. Choose it, and how you usually grade, in Settings.
Letter grades or IB 1 to 7 can show beside the percent, with boundaries you set.
Canvas and Moodle downloads are grouped by student. The Planner works without a setup file, and downloads lessons as PowerPoint with a plain built-in template.
1.5.0: The sidebar says “Not backed up”, in amber, until a folder holds a second copy of your work. Home asks for that folder once.
Go back in time, in Settings: any assignment as it was on an earlier day, restored on its own, with Undo.
Grading Studio can be installed as an app, and it opens with no internet.
A newer version now waits until you click Update now, so nothing changes in the middle of marking.
